Raw hex address 0x1d81080 assigned to bare local `pCVar2`. The decompiler dropped a symbolic reference — either a data-symbol pointer (recover the symbol from the .asm and replace `pCVar2` with symbolic global/array indexing, §11) or a dead code-address store from return-address tracking (delete it, §14). Magic addresses do not survive the relink.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar13` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on its own `actor_name` field (which decays to a pointer), `+ CONST`; `offsetof(actor_name) + CONST*sizeof(elem)` equals the stride of a *different* array the loop reads through `pCVar13`. Replace those `pCVar13->other_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update. (String/buffer-copy cursors that only touch the advanced field are excluded here — those are unrolled_strcpy/unrolled_memcpy.)

Inlined fast sqrt bit-trick (bias `_DAT_01d1a0a4`). Ghidra's numeric `(int)` cast is wrong; the asm reinterprets the float's bit pattern. Bias `_DAT_01d1a0a4` is not a known magic - this may be a sibling-program variant. Confirm against the .asm (SAR/ADD on the float's bits), then express it via a bit-cast helper in a .keep; no named helper is guaranteed to exist in this program.
